chief_complaint: fever, severe sore throat, and swollen neck glands
hpi_details: 25F presents with a 5-day history of extreme fatigue, high fever, and a severely sore throat. She states it hurts to swallow. She has large, tender lumps on both sides of her neck, mostly in the back.
concerns: worried because her throat is so swollen

investigation_events.title: Point-of-care pharyngitis test results
investigation_events.availability_message: The point-of-care pharyngitis test results are now available.

core_concepts: Classic triad: Fever, pharyngitis/tonsillitis, lymphadenopathy (especially posterior cervical).
Splenomegaly occurs in about 50% of cases.
common_misconceptions: Misdiagnosing as Strep pharyngitis and prescribing Amoxicillin, which frequently causes a maculopapular rash in EBV patients.
dangerous_errors: Failing to advise against contact sports, risking splenic rupture.
management_principles: Supportive care. Avoid contact sports for 4 weeks. Monospot test.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) Clinical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 25F with fever, severe fatigue, sore throat, and neck swelling for 5 days.
reference_soap.objective: Exudative tonsillitis. Prominent posterior cervical lymphadenopathy. Mild splenomegaly on palpation.
reference_soap.plan: Monospot test, Rapid Strep (to rule out co-infection). Supportive care (NSAIDs). Strict avoidance of contact sports/heavy lifting for 4 weeks.

learning_objectives: Differentiate EBV mononucleosis from Strep pharyngitis and counsel on splenic rupture risk.

teaching.one_liner: Fever, pharyngitis, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and extreme fatigue typical of EBV infection.
red_flags: Airway compromise from severe tonsillar hypertrophy

must_ask.say: How severe is the sore throat, and is it hard to swallow?
Are the swollen glands mainly at the back of your neck, or elsewhere?
How tired or exhausted do you feel compared to normal?
How high has your fever been, and how many days has it lasted?
Have you had any pain in your upper left belly, or trouble breathing or swallowing?

history.answer: I've had a terrible sore throat and a high fever for the last five days, and my neck is swollen.
It started about five days ago with a slight fever and scratchy throat, but over the last three days it has gotten much worse.
It's about an eight out of ten. The pain is all across the back of my throat on both sides, not just on one side.
It hurts a lot to swallow food and liquids, but I can still swallow my own saliva. I am not drooling.
My breathing is normal, and I don't hear any noisy breathing. My voice sounds a bit muffled because my throat is swollen, but it's not completely hoarse.
No, I can open my mouth fine, though swallowing is very painful.
Yes, I have had high fevers reaching around 38.5 degrees and shaking chills since this began.
No, I don't have a cough, runny nose, nasal congestion, or red eyes.
Yes, I noticed swollen, painful lumps on both sides of my neck, especially towards the back of my neck.
No, I haven't noticed any rash or sandpaper-like roughness on my skin.
Yes, I feel completely exhausted and wiped out. I can barely get out of bed to go to classes.
Now that you mention it, I have felt a slight fullness or mild ache under my ribs on the left side, but no severe belly pain.
No, the pain doesn't shoot up into my ears.
A couple of students in my college dorm had sore throats a couple of weeks ago, but I don't know anyone with the exact same illness.
No, I rarely get sore throats or tonsillitis. This is the first time I've ever felt this sick.
No, I don't have heartburn, acid reflux, or a constant sensation of needing to clear my throat.
I have had the same steady boyfriend for six months. We are sexually active, including oral sex, but no new partners.
I am generally healthy, not immunocompromised, and I have never had any serious chronic medical problems.
I think I might have strep throat because my throat is so red and swollen.
I'm really worried because my throat feels so swollen and I feel so drained that I'm falling behind in school.
I came in hoping to get antibiotics so this infection clears up quickly.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions.
I have never had surgery and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I've been taking over-the-counter ibuprofen every six to eight hours to help take the edge off the throat pain and fever.
No, I don't have any known allergies to penicillin or any other medications.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes or used e-cigarettes.
I drink one or two beers socially on the weekend, but none since I got sick. I don't use any recreational drugs.
I'm a full-time university student, and I live in an on-campus dormitory with a roommate.
My parents and siblings are healthy with no major medical conditions.
My last period started two weeks ago and was normal. I take birth control pills consistently, and there is no chance of pregnancy.

exam.finding: Appears fatigued and moderately ill, sitting comfortably with no respiratory distress or stridor.
Blood pressure 115/75 mmHg, heart rate 96 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 38.6 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Conjunctivae are pink and sclerae are anicteric without injection or pallor.
Bilateral tympanic membranes are clear with normal landmarks and no erythema or effusion.
Bilateral tonsillar enlargement with thick white exudates; uvula is midline with no soft palate deviation.
Prominent, tender posterior cervical lymphadenopathy bilaterally, as well as mild anterior cervical adenopathy.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without wheezing, crackles, or stridor.
Soft, nondistended abdomen with mild tenderness in the left upper quadrant; no guarding or rebound tenderness.
Spleen tip is palpated 2 cm below the left costal margin with mild tenderness; liver edge is not enlarged or tender.
No rash, petechiae, or sandpaper-like lesions on the torso or extremities.
